units.translation: already the affairs of this man are not being valued
In some manuscripts Agenor [Agenor] instead of Pelorus [Pelorus].
The survivors of the sown men (in the battle against Cadmus), as Aeschylus (fr. 385) says, were Chthonius, Udaeus, Pelorus, Hyperenor and Echion.
by no means, in no way.
Of the other form oudama [in no way], about which I have spoken at length in my Lexicon Sophocleum p. 364, there is one example in Aeschylus.
Thus from the copies for koude mē [and not at all].
where oudamēi [in no way] M, as in the manuscripts of other writers too oudamē [in no way] and mēdamē [in no way] is not infrequently written.
where M ou damazetai [is not subdued], which Pauw corrected.
he is maltreated and in no way relaxes from evils
I praise you for these things and will never cease
a secret sailing out was in no way being established
for the dragging never respects the lock of hair

Similarly Soph. Ant. 183 touton oudamou legō [I say this man nowhere], about which Phrynichus in Bekk. Anecd. p. 54, 5 oudamou legō touton [I say this man nowhere]: instead of en oudemiā psēphō tithemai [I place in no vote], oudenos axion logou [worthy of no account].
you would see nowhere the same wing of toil
and without pain there is nowhere a catastrophe
and nowhere a harbor of evils
and someone previously believing in gods nowhere
I say this man nowhere: instead of I place in no vote, worthy of no account
and it is by no means the right time to proclaim this man
by no means being fearless of myself
to me by no means without fear
by no means having acquired a godless named spirit for her children
a report — by no means desirable
for you are more like Libyan women and by no means native ones
I heard the word by no means hospitable
and the fruit is by no means well guarded
O ancestral ground of the Argive land
oude [and not] after an affirmative sentence
oude [and not] after a negative sentence
not even, either alone or joined with other particles, oud' an [not even], all' oude [but not even], oude mēn [nor indeed], oude mē [nor at all] (with second aorist subjunctive), oude per [not even].
where it is placed in an interrogative sentence, as
oud' eti [and no longer], where now ouketi [no longer] from the copies.
where I restored ou dē [not indeed].
thus H. L. Ahrens for ouden lexai prin ōn [to say nothing before being]
before which words one verse is missing to which oude [and not] refers.
The passage is no less defective, where Prien indicated a lacuna.
out' – out' [neither – nor] in Stobaeus, ou bōmos estin [there is no altar] in Stobaeus
Double oude [and not], with ou [not] interposed
where it is more probable oute oute [neither nor], of which the former from the copies, the latter I restored with Blomfield. Nor is oude [and not] more tolerable
te [and] following te [and]. where Hermann restored oute [nor], to which te [and] often responds.
